latest.title: Deploying Amazon Quick Across Independently Governed Organizations: A Multi-Tenant Architecture Guide
latest.description: When multiple organizations share a technology platform but cannot share data, how do you deploy Amazon Quick? This guide evaluates three architectures (Namespaces, Single Account, Hub and Spoke) against data isolation, cost attribution, and regulatory requirements. Includes a decision matrix, governance model, and phased deployment strategy.

latest.title: AWS VPC Lattice Cross-Account Hands-on Guide: Sharing Service Networks Across AWS Accounts Using AWS RAM (Part 2)
latest.description: In Part 1, we built an Amazon VPC Lattice environment to securely connect applications across isolated VPCs without VPC Peering or AWS Transit Gateway. In this guide, we'll extend the setup by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share a VPC Lattice Service Network across AWS accounts. You'll learn how to securely enable cross-account application connectivity while keeping the network architecture simple and scalable.

latest.title: Kubeflow Pipelines vs. Amazon SageMaker Pipelines: A Practical Guide to Choosing the Right MLOps Orchestrator
latest.description: I learned Kubeflow running on our own EKS cluster, then watched a teammate ship the same pipeline in SageMaker with a single decorator. This article is the real answer to the question that followed — not a spec-sheet comparison, covering who owns the infrastructure (you vs. AWS), boilerplate and debugging, deployment, and a decision checklist for each.

latest.title: Your Agent Is Live. Do You Know What It's Doing? (observability for production agents)
latest.description: Your agent passed every eval and it is running in production, but when it breaks at 2 AM, can you see what it did? A practical guide to observability for agentic systems on AWS, covering trajectory tracing, the CloudWatch and Bedrock AgentCore stack, and the four failure modes that never throw an error.

latest.title: The Builder's Guide to Amazon Quick: A Six-Phase Methodology from Discovery to Delivery
latest.description: You open Amazon Quick for the first time and freeze. The possibilities feel infinite, so nothing gets built. This six-phase methodology (Discover, Refine, Design, Build, Test, Iterate) gives you a repeatable framework, with the twist that Amazon Quick itself guides you through every step after discovery. Includes reusable prompts, architecture decision tables, failure mode diagnostics, and a pre-flight checklist.
